header: The railway's own fare table for unreserved second-class travel on ordinary (passenger) services. I use it to give a HINT of the fare on a local (MEMU) train, for which the reservation system holds no fare. SOURCE: Railway Board, Commercial Circular No. 24 of 2025 (No. TC II/2910/2025/Fare, 25 Dec 2025, "Rationalization of basic fare for passenger train services w.e.f. 26.12.2025"), its annexed Passenger Fare Table "Basic fare of ORDINARY SERVICES w.e.f. 26.12.2025": the columns NON-SUBURBAN, SECOND CLASS, "Basic Fare" and "Minimum Chargeable fare", for each slab of distance. I read the circular as a scanned copy (https://www.staffnews.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/CC_24_2025-Revised-Rail-Fare-26-12-2025.pdf, 14 Nov 2026), page 5 and 6 of the annex, and typed it in below. Eastern Railway's Durgapur sections are not the Kolkata SUBURBAN system, so I use the non-suburban column. The circular says: no change for suburban fares and season tickets; rounding "as per existing principles"; GST "as applicable" (none is added to an ordinary ticket here). The ticket price is the "minimum chargeable fare" column: in every row it is the basic fare rounded UP to a multiple of Rs 5, and not less than Rs 10 (the lowest ticket), which is how ordinary tickets are priced (Rs 10, 15, 20...). The test checks that rule on all 80 rows, so a misreading of the scan in either column shows. The table is valid from 26 Dec 2025 until the railway revises it again (ORDINARY_TABLE_EFFECTIVE): a later revision is not known here. The table stops at 500 km (a local train does not run farther); beyond it I give no hint. Rows are written as [last km of the slab, basic fare, minimum chargeable fare]; slabs are 5 km wide to 300 km, then 10 km.

symbols.name: SLABS
symbols.sig: const SLABS: Slab[] = ROWS.map(([to, basic, fare], i) => ({ from: i === 0 ? 1 : ROWS[i - 1][0] + 1, to, basic, fare }))

symbols.name: slabOf
symbols.sig: export function slabOf(km: number): Slab | null
doc: Returns the slab of a whole number of kilometres (1 to 500), or null outside the table.

members.name: km
doc: The distance used, in whole km (the source's distance, rounded).

members.name: low
doc: The lowest and highest fare over the uncertainty of the distance; they are equal when no fare step lies within it.

members.name: slabs
doc: The table slabs the range touches (one, or two or more when the range crosses a step).

members.name: tolerance
doc: The km either way the distance may be out by.

symbols.name: fareHint
symbols.sig: export function fareHint(distanceKm: number): FareHint | null
doc: The HINT for a distance in km as RailRadar gives it. RailRadar's cumulative distances differ from the railway's own tariff distances by a little (0.4 to 6.5 km on the four trains checked on 14 Nov 2026), so I work out the fare for the distance and for the distance less and more than a TOLERANCE (2 km, or 1% of the distance if more). If the fares differ, I give both (a range), never a single figure that may be a step out. Null when the distance is not a usable number or the range passes the end of the table (500 km).

behaviours: the slabs run without a gap from 1 km to 500 km: 5 km wide to 300 km, then 10 km
in EVERY row the ticket fare is the basic fare rounded up to a multiple of Rs 5, and not under Rs 10 (the lowest ticket): a slip in reading either column of the scan would show here
fares never fall as the distance grows (basic and ticket)
the revision of 26 Dec 2025 shows: no step up to 215 km; the first slab after it (216-220) is Rs 55 against Rs 45 for 211-215
figures read straight off the table: 1-5 km Rs 10 (basic 3); 41-45 km Rs 10; 46-50 km Rs 15; 100 km Rs 25; 156-160 km Rs 35; 300 km Rs 65; 301-310 km Rs 70; 500 km Rs 100
a distance outside the table, or not a whole number of km, has no slab
Durgapur to Asansol, 42.3 km: Rs 10, one figure (the slab 41-45 km holds the whole uncertainty of 40-44 km: 36-40 is Rs 10 as well)
Durgapur to Howrah side, 158 km (tolerance 2 km): 156-160 km is one slab, Rs 35 only
when the uncertainty crosses a fare step the hint is a RANGE: 160.5 km could be 158.5-162.5 km, slabs 156-160 (Rs 35) and 161-165 (Rs 40): Rs 35 to 40, with both slabs named
the tolerance is 2 km, or 1% of the distance when that is more (300 km: 3 km)
a distance whose range passes the end of the table (499 km, tolerance 5) has no hint; nor has zero, a negative, NaN or Infinity
the shortest trips cost the minimum ticket: 3 km is Rs 10, 0.5 km is Rs 10
a range crossing 215 km shows the revision's step: 214 km gives Rs 45 to 55
